title: research/window-break-even-4470: short label windows under the #4470 invoice vs the Theorem B line cap (no new kappa)
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"Matarener"} -->
_Requested by **Mark**_

## Change and mathematical scope

**Optimistic model screen. No new κ, no supplier, no native word.** Package `research/window-break-even-4470`.

Under the productive-helper accounting of the selected #4470 word, a shorter label window h (fresh block d = h − 1) lowers the cost a line system may pay per line. It also raises the lines per dimension the system needs. For dense units with one deleted frame (the case of every built complex supplier), h = 3, 4, 5 and 7 need more lines per dimension than the proven Theorem B cap v/T ≤ 2^k′ + 1 of `line-system-saturation` allows, and h = 6 misses by about 2%. So "fewer fresh axes" does not pay by itself. The live cells are the even windows h = 6 and h = 8, and deleting more than one frame.

- `verify.py` rebuilds the #4470 targets and paid histograms **exactly** from `joint-helper-lattice/RESULT.json`. The root is 0.003020165977.
- It generalises the invoice to a line system (v, T, h, D, k deleted lines): ports v − k, centre D − k paid as T jobs (the E8 floor 72 − k), the same #4440 controller, and the #4470 local word scaled by V/112 in counts and d/8 in ranks. The surplus is exactly S = (p+2)(v − D) − V (checked in exact arithmetic).
- Named systems as a multiple of the record: E7 0.710 (0.825 with two frames deleted), E6/D4/D5/D6/Z8 0, E8+A3 0.238, D16⁺ 0.565 (Delsarte cap 0.649), D24⁺ 0.130.
- At the Theorem B cap: h = 6 gives 0.980 / 1.166 / 1.435 for k = T / 2T / 3T, h = 7 gives 0.710 / 0.825 / 0.983, and h = 8 gives 1.460 or more. At k′ ≤ 2 a saturated dense unit has D = v and no saving at all.
- Break-even v/T for k = T, needed vs cap: h = 7: 10.06 vs 9, h = 8: 12.36 vs 16, h = 11: 21.7 vs 33 (best known 12.7). Nothing ties at h ≥ 21.

Remaining obligations, all outside this package: a native word with free central shears for any new unit, its real local profile (the scaled word is a proxy), sparser pairings, and the BIT side.

## Task and overlap

Base `ff3cc58e3`. Card `complex-new-helper-inventory`, scope **refined**: the earlier line-system screens (#2244 `line-system-saturation` x\*(h), #2873, discussion #3622) used the pre-#4359 break-even fit. This package re-prices the window question under the #4470 invoice. `find_overlap.py` (open PRs and discussions refreshed 2026-10-23, closed PRs from a 2026-10-18 cache) found no such re-pricing.

## Validation

```sh
python3.12 scripts/research_package.py --package research/window-break-even-4470 --check-only
python3.12 scripts/research_package.py --package research/window-break-even-4470
python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/window-break-even-4470 --check-source-history
```

All three PASS locally (Windows, CPython 3.12, standard library only). The verifier takes about 3 minutes and replays `RESULT.json`. `test_verify.py` has rejecting controls (a changed helper count, a dropped centre, a wrong pair count) and positive controls (a tie unit has no saving, monotone in v/T, the Theorem B caps, the root near S/G). This is a model screen, not a lower bound.

## Credit

It uses the #4470 invoice of `joint-helper-lattice` (zxv's native supplier, the PR4440/PR4441/PR4447 contributions and the other authors credited there), the cost table of `char2-threshold`, and the Theorem B cap and constructions of `line-system-saturation`. All are referenced unchanged. Prepared with substantial Claude Code assistance.

## Open next questions

1. Does a saturated even-window system exist at h = 6 (v = 8T) or h = 8 (v = 16T)? These are the only short windows whose cap clears the record here.
2. Is the centre floor D − k attainable beyond one deleted frame? The h = 6 and h = 7 verdicts depend on it.
